message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you set). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + action cards). 8 “Draw Two,” 8 “Skip,” 8 “Reverse,” 4 “Wild,” 4 “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the rest face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1️⃣ Play a card that matches either color or number (or an action card). 2️⃣ If you can’t play, draw one card. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Action Cards** | • **Draw Two** – next player draws two and skips.
• **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four and skips (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you’re down to one card, shout “UNO!” before your opponent’s turn starts. If you forget and someone catches you, you must draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | First to zero cards wins the round. Score: sum of all cards left in opponents’ hands (number cards = face value, action cards = 20, Wild = 50). | | **Game End** | First to reach 500 points (or agreed total) wins the game. | **Tips & Variations** * **Stacking** – Some house rules allow stacking Draw Twos or Draw Fours (e.g., if you play a Draw Two and the next player also has a Draw Two, they can stack it instead of drawing). * **No Draw Four Rule** – In some variations, you can play a Wild Draw Four even if you have a matching color; if challenged and found wrong, you must draw four. * **Custom Decks** – You can add extra Wild cards or create themed decks. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the rules to suit your group.
